_comment: Carry destination for R9-UX-5 (#1795, lane UX: advisor actions and exact idle sub-codes), from R9-UX-1 (#1795, why now, why not) and R9-UX-2 (#1795, advisor inbox).
The round-9 roster's R9-UX-5 group brief on handoff/audit-r9-fixplan should carry the same text; the roster is not on main,
so this file is the in-tree destination. While the two disagree the newer one is right. Shape: .claude/rules/finding-propagation.md.
stage: R9-UX-5, or any later seat that adds lines to the chart's hover tooltip (tooltipHtml, idleWhyHtml) or turns an advisor inbox row into an apply action (advisorRows, attachAdvisorInbox); and R9-UX-7 (model status and diagnostics, which adds to the Health tab), see the third entry

carries.from: the pull request for R9-UX-1, which put the idle step's likely-because block in the tooltip
carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control in tests/card_browser.mjs's P9 grid, in Chromium. With the tooltip capped at the chart's height by max-height and overflow: hidden, the check 'P9 grid: no text is clipped where its ancestor cannot scroll to it' went red on the explanation's li runs in the tooltip_hover cell; the same grid is green with fitWhy, which omits the explanation's last lines instead (the control). Without either, the box ran below the chart on a 400 px card (a probe measured the box's bottom past the chart wrapper's), which the P9 pop-up check did not see because it bounded a tooltip by its chart horizontally only.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust these figures: they were measured at the UX-1 code head, and a later stage is judged against its own merge base. Run tests/card_browser.mjs and read the two P9 checks named here; then hover the dearest idle step on a narrow card and compare the tooltip's box with its .chartwrap's.
carries.brief: The hover tooltip cannot scroll, so it may not clip text (P9 refuses overflow: hidden on it), and since R9-UX-1 the P9 pop-up check also holds a tooltip inside its chart's height. Exact idle sub-codes replace the likely-because lines in idleWhyHtml rather than adding a second block, and anything that does not fit is omitted by fitWhy, last line first, never clipped. Put the most telling line first, because on a small card it is the one that survives.

carries.from: the pull request for R9-UX-2, which put the advisor inbox on the Advisor tab
carries.control: Established by tests/card.mjs's scenario 'the advisor inbox (R9-UX-2, #1795)': the hot-water row has act open_schedule, which only sets dialog.page to plan and calls no service (check 'the hot-water row opens the schedule editor, and calls no service'). Null control: the valve row's apply_valve calls assign_entity with a manual setpoint, so a row that applies something is already pinned there.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust this description of the code: read advisorRows and attachAdvisorInbox in the card at your merge base and run node tests/card.mjs; the hot-water check above is the one that must change.
carries.brief: R9-UX-5 turns the hot-water row's Open schedule action into an apply action: the row's act becomes a service call that writes the recommended setpoint, the Plan-page fallback goes, and the check that the row calls no service is rewritten to pin the call. Price of a degree is delivered by R9-UX-2 as the degree row, whose action opens the what-if panel seeded with the tile's target; nothing is owed on it. A hot-water price is interpolated linearly between the swept candidates (dhwCostPerDay) because the default setpoint is off the sweep's grid; an apply action must write the recommended setpoint, not an interpolated one.

carries.from: the pull request for R9-UX-3, which put the Health tab on the card
carries.control: Established by tests/card.mjs's scenario 'the Health tab (R9-UX-3)': the card lists a waiting sensor from its unavailable state and a fixed per-sensor reason (HEALTH_WAITING), because Home Assistant publishes no attributes for an unavailable entity, so waiting_for is unreadable by the card at the moment it matters. Null control: with the sensor available the row does not appear, and the card reads nothing from the unavailable sensor's attributes.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust this description of the code: read healthPageHtml and HEALTH_WAITING in the card at your merge base and run node tests/card.mjs. Three facts the Health tab could not read, each re-checked at your merge base: the plan's fallback input ('the plan uses X instead') is not published; a count of insight sensors that are off by default has no card-side source (the card has no entity registry, and tests/entities.py refuses card reads of disabled-by-default sensors); the Input Problem sensor's limit (max_age_minutes) is published only for a failing input.
carries.brief: R9-UX-7 adds model status to the Health tab and must not expect waiting_for from an unavailable sensor: if it needs the reason in words it publishes it on an always-available enabled sensor (a per-sensor map, or a field on an existing one), or keeps the card's per-sensor reason map in step with any sensor it adds to HEALTH_WAITING. A row that needs the fallback input, the default-off insight count or the limit of a healthy input needs the backend to publish it first; the Health tab shows those rows as plain text today and says so in docs/dashboard-card.md. Where this entry and the roster's R9-UX-7 brief disagree, the newer is right and the other is the bug.
